blocks.text: The Sutra Praising the Buddha's Reception of the Pure Land

inline.s: Translated by command by the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang of the Tang dynasty
Note: The headings in the sections below belong to the outline, not to the scripture itself.
Thus have I heard: at one time the Bhagavan dwelt in Shravasti, in the Jetavana Grove of Anathapindada's park.
Together with the great bhikshus
(monks)

in a multitude of twelve hundred and fifty. They were all revered elders among the hearers, well known and recognized by the assembly, great arhats. Their names were: the Venerable Shariputra, Mahamaudgalyayana, Mahakashyapa, and Aniruddha. Such great hearers as these were the foremost.

Moreover, together with countless bodhisattva mahasattvas, all abiding in the stage of non-regression, adorned with immeasurable merit. Their names were: the Bodhisattva Manjushri, the Bodhisattva Aparajita, the Bodhisattva Ever-Vigorous, and the Bodhisattva Never-Resting. Such great bodhisattvas as these were the foremost.

Moreover, there were Shakra, the great Brahma King, lord of the Saha world, and the four world-guardian kings, as the foremost. Hundreds of thousands of kotis and nayutas of heavenly hosts, together with the world's countless gods, humans, and asuras
(asuras)
and others, all gathered and took their seats in the assembly to hear the Dharma.

At that time the World-Honoured One said to Shariputra: Do you know this? To the west of this world, passing over hundreds of thousands of kotis and nayutas of buddha-lands, there is a buddha-world called Sukhavati, the Land of Utmost Bliss. The World-Honoured One there is named Amitayus, the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, as well as Amitabha, the Buddha of Immeasurable Light, Tathagata, Arhat, Perfectly Enlightened One, complete in the ten titles. He is now dwelling there, abiding in peace and ease, and for the sake of all sentient beings he proclaims the profound and subtle Dharma, causing them to attain supreme benefit and joy.

Moreover, Shariputra, for what reason and on what cause is that buddha-world called Sukhavati? Shariputra, because in that world all sentient beings have no suffering or distress of body or mind whatsoever, but only immeasurable purity, joy, and happiness. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

blocks.text: (2) The Adornments of the Environmental Reward

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati, in every place there are seven rows of wonderful jewel balustrades, seven rows of jeweled tala trees, and seven rows of wonderfully jeweled netting, surrounding it on all sides, adorned with four kinds of jewels, gold, silver, vaidurya, and sphatika, beautifully inlaid and graced. Shariputra, in that buddha-land there are such wondrous ornaments and adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati, in every place there are seven wonderful jeweled ponds, filled with the water of eight virtues. What are the eight virtues of this water? First, it is pure and clear. Second, it is cool and refreshing. Third, it is sweet and fine. Fourth, it is light and soft. Fifth, it is moistening and enriching. Sixth, it is calm and harmonious. Seventh, when drunk it removes the immeasurable afflictions of hunger and thirst and the like. Eighth, having drunk it, it surely nourishes the faculties and the four great elements and increases manifold supreme wholesome roots. Beings rich in merit always delight in its enjoyment.

These jeweled ponds have golden sands spread over their bottoms. On all four sides there are stairways and paths, adorned with four kinds of jewels, most lovely and delightful. Around the ponds are wonderful jeweled trees, arranged in rows and inlaid with ornament, their fragrance rich and penetrating, adorned with the seven jewels, most lovely and delightful. As for the seven jewels: first, gold; second, silver; third, vaidurya; fourth, sphatika; fifth, red pearls; sixth, ashmagarbha jewels; and seventh, musaragalva jewels.

In these ponds there are always manifold lotus flowers of varied colors, as large as chariot wheels: blue in form and blue in hue, with blue light and blue reflection; yellow in form and yellow in hue, with yellow light and yellow reflection; red in form and red in hue, with red light and red reflection; white in form and white in hue, with white light and white reflection, four forms, four hues, four lights, four reflections. Shariputra, in that buddha-land there are such wondrous ornaments and adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati there naturally arises always the immeasurable, boundless music of manifold wondrous instruments, its tones and melodies harmonious and elegant, most lovely and delightful. When sentient beings hear these wondrous sounds, all their evil afflictions are wholly extinguished, and immeasurable wholesome dharmas gradually increase, until they quickly realize supreme and perfect enlightenment. Shariputra, in that buddha-land there are such wondrous ornaments and adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

blocks.text: 6. The Great Earth of Pure Gold

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati, the great earth is everywhere formed of genuine gold. Its touch is soft, its fragrance pure, its radiance bright; immeasurable and boundless, it is inlaid with wonderful jewels. Shariputra, in that buddha-land there are such wondrous ornaments and adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

blocks.text: 7. The Constant Rain of Heavenly Flowers

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati, throughout the six periods of day and night there constantly rains every kind of supreme, wonderful heavenly flower, radiant and lustrous, fragrant and clean, delicate and soft, of varied colors. Although it delights the body and mind of all who see it, it gives rise to no clinging, and it increases the immeasurable, countless, inconceivable supreme merit of sentient beings. Those beings, throughout the six periods of day and night, constantly hold them in offering to the Buddha Amitayus. Each morning, taking these heavenly flowers, within the time of a meal they fly to immeasurable worlds in other directions and offer them to hundreds of thousands of kotis of buddhas. At the seat of each buddha they scatter and offer hundreds of thousands of kotis of tree-flowers. Then they return to their own abode to sport therein. Shariputra, in that buddha-land there are such wondrous ornaments and adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

blocks.text: 8. The Flock of Birds Proclaiming the Dharma

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati there are always various kinds of wonderful, lovely, and delightful birds of many colors, such as geese, wild geese, herons, egrets, swans, cranes, peacocks, parrots, kalavinkas, and the twin-hearted birds, and so forth. Such flocks of birds, throughout the six periods of day and night, always gather together and send forth harmonious and elegant sounds. According to the voice of their kind they proclaim the wonderful Dharma, the profound stations of mindfulness, the right endeavors, the bases of psychic power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, the path-branches, and other immeasurable wonderful dharmas. When the sentient beings of that land hear these sounds, each attains the immeasurable merit of recollecting the Buddha, recollecting the Dharma, and recollecting the Sangha, and they are permeated and cultivated thereby. Shariputra, what do you think? Are those birds of that land beings of the animal realm in an evil destiny? Do not think so! Why? In that pure buddha-land there are no three evil destinies; it does not even hear the name of the three evil realms, much less have actual beings such as these birds, born of karmic offenses. Know that they are all transformations made by the Buddha Amitayus, causing them to proclaim the immeasurable sound of Dharma and to work for the benefit and happiness of all sentient beings. Shariputra, in that buddha-land there are such wondrous ornaments and adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

blocks.text: 9. The Wondrous Wind Proclaiming the Dharma

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati there is always a wondrous wind that blows upon the jeweled trees and the jeweled netting, producing subtle and wonderful sounds. It is as though hundreds of thousands of kotis of heavenly instruments were sounding together at once, producing subtle and sweet sounds most lovely and delightful. Thus in that land there is always a wondrous wind blowing upon the multitude of jeweled trees and the jeweled netting, striking forth a variety of subtle sounds that proclaim the various dharmas. When the sentient beings of that land hear these sounds, they awaken the recollection of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha and mindful attention to them, together with immeasurable merit. Shariputra, in that buddha-land there are such wondrous ornaments and adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati there are such immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and most wondrous things. Even if one passed through hundreds of thousands of kotis and nayutas of kalpas, and with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of kotis and nayutas of tongues, each tongue uttering immeasurable sounds, praised its merits, one could never exhaust them. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

blocks.text: (3) The Adornments of the Direct Reward

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati, for what reason is the Buddha called Amitayus, Immeasurable Life? Shariputra, because that Tathagata and the sentient beings there have a lifespan of immeasurable, countless great kalpas. For this reason the Tathagata of that land is called Amitayus. Shariputra, it has been ten great kalpas since the Buddha Amitayus realized anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Shariputra, for what reason is that Buddha called Amitabha, Immeasurable Light? Shariputra, because that Tathagata constantly emits immeasurable, boundless wonderful light, universally illumining all the buddha-lands in the ten directions and carrying on the buddha-work without obstruction. For this reason the Tathagata of that land is called Amitabha. Shariputra, that pure buddha-land accomplishes such adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati the Buddha Amitayus always has immeasurable hearer disciples, all of them great arhats, endowed with every kind of subtle and sublime merit; their number is boundless and cannot be reckoned. Shariputra, that pure buddha-land accomplishes such adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the pure buddha-land of Sukhavati the Buddha Amitayus always has immeasurable bodhisattva disciples, all of them bound for a single lifetime, endowed with every kind of subtle and sublime merit; their number is boundless and cannot be reckoned. Even if one passed through countless kalpas praising their merits, one could never exhaust them. Shariputra, that buddha-land accomplishes such adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

Moreover, Shariputra, if sentient beings are born in that land, they all become non-regressing, never again falling into the perilous evil destinies, the border regions, or the lowly and contemptible mleccha class; they always roam among the pure buddha-lands of the buddhas, their supreme practices and vows advancing in thought after thought, and they are certain to realize anuttara-samyak-sambodhi. Shariputra, that buddha-land accomplishes such adornments of merit, most lovely and delightful. Therefore it is called the world of Sukhavati.

Moreover, Shariputra, if sentient beings hear of that pure buddha-land of the Buddha Amitayus in the west, adorned with the assembly of immeasurable merit, they should all make the vow to be born in that buddha-land. Why is that? Because if they are born there, they gather together in the same assembly with those great beings of immeasurable merit and manifold adornments, and enjoy that pure buddha-land of immeasurable merit and manifold adornments, the happiness of the Great Vehicle, ever without regression, their immeasurable practices and vows advancing thought after thought, quickly realizing supreme and perfect enlightenment.

Shariputra, the sentient beings who are born in that buddha-land accomplish immeasurable, boundless merit. It is not sentient beings with few good roots who are able to be reborn in the pure buddha-land of the Sukhavati world of the Buddha Amitayus.

Moreover, Shariputra, if a good man or good woman of pure faith hears the name of the Buddha Amitayus with its immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merit and virtue, and the merit and adornments of the Sukhavati world, and upon hearing it thinks upon it: if for one day and night, or two, or three, or four, or five, or six, or seven, they fix their mind without distraction, then at the end of their life the Buddha Amitayus, together with his immeasurable hearer disciples and bodhisattvas, surrounds them at the front and rear, comes and stands before them, and adds his compassionate protection, causing their mind not to be distracted. Having laid down their life, they follow the Buddha and his assembly and are born in the pure buddha-land of the Sukhavati world of Amitayus.

Moreover, Shariputra, observing this great matter of benefit and happiness, I speak the truthful and sincere words: if any good men or good women of pure faith hear of this inconceivable merit of the Buddha Amitayus and the pure buddha-land of the Sukhavati world, they should all believe, accept, and make the vow, and practise accordingly, to be born in that buddha-land.

blocks.text: 4. The Praise of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, as I now praise and extol the Buddha Amitayus and the immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable merit of his buddha-land, in the same way in the east there are also the present Akshobhya Tathagata, the Mountain-Banner Tathagata, the Great Mountain Tathagata, the Mountain-Light Tathagata, the Wonderful-Banner Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the ji
jing
ga
jia

sha sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the east. Each one manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way in the south there are also the present Sun-Moon-Light Tathagata, the Name-Light Tathagata, the Great-Light-Accumulation Tathagata, the Meru-Light Tathagata, the Boundless-Vigor Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the south. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way in the west there are also the present Amitayus Tathagata, the Immeasurable-Skandha Tathagata, the Amitabha Tathagata, the Immeasurable-Banner Tathagata, the Great-Free Tathagata, the Great-Light Tathagata, the Light-Blaze Tathagata, the Great-Jewel-Banner Tathagata, the Emitting-Light Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the west. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way in the north there are also the present Immeasurable-Light-Adorned Tathagata of the Realization of Penetrating Wisdom, the Immeasurable-Heavenly-Drum-Trembling-with-Great-Wonderful-Sound Tathagata, the Great-Accumulation Tathagata, the Light-Net Tathagata, the Sala Emperor Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the north. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way below there are also the present Tathagata Revealing the True Principle of All Wondrous Dharmas and Constantly Emitting the Supreme Light of the King of Fire's Merits, the Lion Tathagata, the Name Tathagata, the Praise-Light Tathagata, the True Dharma Tathagata, the Wondrous Dharma Tathagata, the Dharma-Banner Tathagata, the Merit-Friend Tathagata, the Merit-Title Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands below. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way above there are also the present Brahma-Sound Tathagata, the Constellation-King Tathagata, the Fragrance-Light Tathagata, the Tathagata of the Supreme Merit of the Red Lotus, the Tathagata Revealing All Benefit, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands above. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way in the south-east there are also the present Supreme and Vast Cloud-Thunder-Sound King Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the south-east. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way in the south-west there are also the present Supreme Sun-Light Name-Merit Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the south-west. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way in the north-west there are also the present Immeasurable-Merit Fire-King Light Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the north-west. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

Moreover, Shariputra, in the same way in the north-east there are also the present Countless Hundred-Thousand-Koti Vast-Wisdom Tathagata, and such buddhas, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, abiding in their own pure buddha-lands in the north-east. Each manifests the broad and long tongue, covering the three-thousand-great-thousand world on all sides, and speaks the truthful words: All you sentient beings should believe and accept this Dharma-gate of praising the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land, the Dharma-gate of reception by all the buddhas.

blocks.text: 5. The Reception by All the Buddhas

inline.s: Moreover, Shariputra, for what reason is this sutra named 'The Dharma-gate of Praising the Inconceivable Merit of the Buddha-Land and Reception by All the Buddhas'? Shariputra, because in this sutra I extol and praise the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land of the Sukhavati world of the Buddha Amitayus, and the Buddhas and World-Honoured Ones of the ten directions, in order to conveniently benefit and bring happiness to sentient beings, each abiding in his own land, manifesting great spiritual transformations and speaking the truthful words, urging sentient beings to believe and accept this Dharma. Therefore this sutra is named 'The Dharma-gate of Praising the Inconceivable Merit of the Buddha-Land and Reception by All the Buddhas.'

Moreover, Shariputra, whether a good man or good woman has already heard, will hear, or now hears this sutra, upon hearing it they should deeply generate faith and understanding. Having generated faith and understanding, they are certain to be received by the Buddhas and World-Honoured Ones who dwell in the ten directions, as many as ten Ganges-sands. Those who practise as instructed are all certain to reach non-regression with regard to anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and are all certain to be born in the pure buddha-land of the Sukhavati world of the Buddha Amitayus. Therefore, Shariputra, all you sentient beings should believe, accept, and comprehend the words of me and the Buddhas and World-Honoured Ones of the ten directions; you should diligently strive and practise as told, and not entertain any doubt.

Moreover, Shariputra, if a good man or good woman, with regard to the merit and adornments of the pure buddha-land of the Sukhavati world of Amitayus, has already made the vow, will make the vow, or now makes the vow, they are certain to be received by the Buddhas and World-Honoured Ones who dwell in the ten directions, as many as ten Ganges-sands. Those who practise as instructed are all certain to reach non-regression with regard to anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and are all certain to be born in the pure buddha-land of the Sukhavati world of the Buddha Amitayus. Therefore, Shariputra, if there are good men or good women of pure faith, they should all, with deep faith and understanding in the pure buddha-land of the Sukhavati world of Amitayus, make the vow to be born there, and not act indolently.

Moreover, Shariputra, as I now extol the buddhas and praise the Buddha Amitayus and the inconceivable merit of the buddha-land of the Sukhavati world, in the same way the Buddhas and World-Honoured Ones of the ten directions praise my inconceivable, boundless merit, all saying: How wondrous and rare! Śākyamuni the Tranquil, Śākyamuni the Dharma-King, Tathagata, Arhat, Perfectly Enlightened One, Complete in Bright Conduct, Well-Gone, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Tamer, Charioteer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha and World-Honoured One, is able in this Saha world, in this evil age of the five defilements, namely the defilement of the kalpa, the defilement of sentient beings, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of views, and the defilement of life, to realize anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and, in order to conveniently benefit and bring happiness to sentient beings, to speak this Dharma that is supremely hard to believe in this world. Therefore, Shariputra, know that I now, in this defiled Saha world, in this evil age of the five defilements, have realized anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, and, in order to conveniently benefit and bring happiness to sentient beings, have spoken this Dharma supremely hard to believe in this world, most wondrous, most rare, and inconceivable!

Moreover, Shariputra, in this defiled Saha world, in this evil age of the five defilements, if there are good men or good women of pure faith who, upon hearing this supremely hard-to-believe Dharma of the whole world, can generate faith and understanding, receive and hold it, proclaim it, and practise as taught, know that such a person is most rare, having planted good roots in the presence of immeasurable buddhas. When such a person's life ends, they are certain to be born in the Pure Land of Sukhavati in the west, and to enjoy that pure buddha-land adorned with manifold merits, the happiness of the Great Vehicle. Day and night, throughout the six periods, they draw near, attend, and make offerings to the Buddha Amitayus. They travel through the ten directions and make offerings to the buddhas. At the seat of each buddha they hear the Dharma and receive the prophecy; their provisions of merit and wisdom swiftly become complete, and they quickly realize supreme and perfect enlightenment.

At that time, when the Bhagavan had spoken this sutra, the Venerable Shariputra and the other great hearers, together with the host of bodhisattva mahasattvas, the immeasurable gods, humans, and asuras, and the entire assembly, hearing what the Buddha had said, were all filled with great joy and, with faith, accepted and practised it.
